newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA CENTRAL BANK SAYS NO INTERVENTION IN PESO.
newsitem.headline: MANILA CENTRAL BANK SAYS NO INTERVENTION IN PESO.

text.p: The Philippine central bank said on Thursday it did not intervene in the foreign exchange market despite the peso being under pressure on account of turmoil in the region's currency markets.
"The central bank has purposely stayed out of active intervention. I am conserving my ammunition," central bank governor Gabriel Singson told reporters.
"What is happening now is that banks are trading among themselves. That's why we see a big volume," Singson said.
He said the weakness in the peso was not as big as the other currencies in the region.
"The rate of depreciation of the peso is still slower than the depreciation of the currencies of other economies perceived to be stronger," he said.
The peso settled at 26.49 to dollar from the previous close of 29.49. But it fell to as low as 29.62 in the morning. Volume was higher at $150.8 million from $62.55 million.
